questions.solution_text:

$2(1 - \cos^2 x) - 3\cos x = 0$
$2 - 2\cos^2 x - 3\cos x = 0$
$2\cos^2 x + 3\cos x - 2 = 0$
$(2\cos x - 1)(\cos x + 2) = 0$
$\cos x = \dfrac{1}{2}$ or $\cos x = -2$
Since $-1 \le \cos x \le 1$, $\cos x = -2$ has no real solutions.
When $\cos x = \dfrac{1}{2}$:
